This stable release rolls up dev pre-releases v2.81-dev … v2.84-dev.

## Fixed

### Backup and restore

- **Restoring a full backup deleted every user account and restored none — then
  reported success.** Backups have always been written with password hashes
  stripped out, but the restore only re-created accounts that *had* a password
  hash. Since none ever did, a restore deleted the whole user table and put
  nothing back: every account, role and company assignment gone, the system
  dropped to zero users, and the app fell back to the first-run setup wizard.
  The response still said the restore had succeeded, so nothing looked wrong
  until someone tried to sign in. If a backup can't restore accounts, it now
  leaves the existing ones alone and says so.
- **Restoring a backup from the Saved Backups list failed completely.** That
  path had the same code as the upload restore but without the check above, so
  any saved backup containing at least one user hit a database error, rolled the
  whole restore back, and returned only "Restore failed" — and it is the path
  scheduled backups feed, so it was broken in exactly the situation it exists
  for. Both restores now run the same code and can't drift apart again.
- **Companies and per-user company access were never backed up at all.** A
  restore could therefore not rebuild who can see which company, and student
  records depended on the companies happening to already exist on the target
  system with the same internal ids. Both are now included, and companies are
  matched by name so a restore works even when two systems number them
  differently.

### Help and on-screen wording

- **Words running together in the help pages.** Throughout the help, a bold or
  code-styled word could run straight into the word after it — "Click
  **View**on any row", "pressing **Back**restores the list", "make
  sure`X-Forwarded-Proto`". The cause turned out to be the compiler rather than
  the wording: whenever a sentence contained a typographic character (a curly
  apostrophe, an em dash, smart quotes, an arrow) the build silently dropped the
  space following the nearest highlighted word. The text had been written
  correctly all along, which is why the fault appeared in seemingly random
  places and could not be spotted by reading the source.

  **182** occurrences across all 29 help pages are now fixed and pinned so the
  compiler cannot drop them again, verified by compiling the help the same way
  the production build does and confirming no highlighted word is left touching
  the next one. Five more outside the help system were corrected too: the
  first/last name note on the Import page, two lines on the Backup page about
  what a portable backup contains, and the imported-file summary on the Import
  Aliases tab.

- Fifteen places where the space had been tucked *inside* the highlighted word,
  so it rendered bold or in the code font — most visibly a code chip reading
  " Color" with a gap inside its grey background. The spaces now sit outside the
  highlight.

### Report exports

- A section heading in a multi-section PDF could be stranded at the foot of one
  page with its content on the next.
- A tall image in a PDF ran off the bottom of the page instead of being scaled
  to fit, and sat against the left margin instead of centred.
- A PDF made up only of charts chose portrait orientation, because the layout
  was decided purely from table column counts.
- The Export menu now closes when you click away from it.

## Added

- **Report PDFs can now include their charts.** Every report's **Export** menu
  has a new **Include charts in PDF** tickbox, on by default. With it ticked, a
  PDF opens with pictures of the report's charts — in the order they appear on
  screen — followed by the usual data table. Untick it for a data-only PDF; your
  choice is remembered on your device. The charts reflect whatever filters,
  grouping and dates are in force when you export, and a panel showing no data
  is left out rather than exported as an empty box.

- **Charts always print on a light background**, whichever theme you use, so a
  report exported in dark mode looks the same as one exported in light mode. In
  dark mode you'll see the charts flick to light for a moment while the file is
  prepared — that's the capture, and it puts itself back.

- **"Include user credentials" when creating a backup.** Off by default. With
  it, the archive carries the password hashes and MFA secrets a restore needs to
  bring accounts back on a rebuilt server — so it is only offered for an archive
  that will actually be encrypted (a standard backup needs `ENCRYPTION_KEY` set;
  a portable backup is always passphrase-encrypted). Such a file is equivalent
  to the password database, so store it accordingly. Scheduled backups have the
  same option in the Automatic Backups panel.

- MFA secrets are re-encrypted with the target system's key during a restore, so
  a portable backup restored onto a machine with a different encryption key
  leaves multi-factor sign-in working instead of locking those users out.

- A restore that would leave the system with **no enabled SuperAdmin** is now
  refused before anything is changed, rather than completing and locking
  everyone out of administration.

## Updated

- **The restore result now tells you what happened to user accounts** — how many
  the archive held, how many were restored and how many were skipped, plus the
  companies and access assignments — and shows an amber warning rather than a
  green tick when no accounts could be restored.
- Restoring accounts now signs you out, because the restored accounts aren't the
  ones the current session was issued for. Sign in again with an account from
  the backup.
- Companies are never deleted during a restore. One already present is reused
  and one that's missing is created, so scheduled exports, offerings and
  API-key grants pointing at them are left intact.
- Report PDFs are laid out by the same generator the whole-page report export
  uses, so they gain a proper document title and a heading above the data table.
  Previously the title was derived from the filename. **CSV and Excel exports
  are unchanged** — same columns, same values, same sheet layout — so anything
  that consumes them, including scheduled exports, carries on working exactly as
  before.

## Notes

Charts in exports are a PDF-only feature. CSV is plain text and cannot hold a
picture, and the spreadsheet writer used for `.xlsx` files cannot embed one, so
those formats ignore the setting. It also applies only to exports you run from
the browser — **scheduled exports** (email, Google Drive, Box, OneDrive) are
generated on the server, where there is no browser to draw a chart in, so they
remain tabular.

## For anyone reading the API directly

`counts.users` in the restore response changed from a plain number (which
reported the archive's row count, not what was actually restored — the reason
the data loss went unnoticed) to `{ inArchive, restored, skipped }`.
`counts.companies` and `counts.userCompanies` are new.
